To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) Invasive Streptococcus Pyogenes infections in adults and children differ in terms of epidemiology, clinical presentation and antibiotic susceptibility; 2) The two most frequent emm-types, emm-1 and emm-12, differ in terms of antibiotic resistance, clinical manifestations and age distribution.

Invasive Streptococcus Pyogenes infections in children were mainly caused by strains of emm type 1 and were associated with pharyngotnsillitis and varicella, and in adults by emm type 12 and were associated with diabetes mellitus, malignancy and intravenous drug abuse.

the epidemiology of invasive GAS infections is different between children and adults and this difference is important for designing prevention strategies.
